extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners (primary); patent applicants and practitioners as secondary readers
extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO examiner guidance on issuing notices/decisions, claim-by-claim examination, disclosure/citation of prior art, extensions, written arguments, and treatment of amendments during substantive and formality examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final Notice of Grounds for Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where grounds for rejection exist (including where grounds remain after amendments) or where grounds are established for reasons other than amendments, an examiner shall issue a non-final notice of grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if after amendments a foreigner loses patent eligibility under Article 25 this is a non-final notice since it arises not from the amendment itself. Also, when an examiner rediscovers a ground after re-examination that does not meet the final-notice criteria, issue non-final. If uncertainty exists between final and non-final, issue non-final to avoid unreasonably limiting applicant's opportunity to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Notice of Grounds for Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A final notice of grounds for rejection is issued when a ground for rejection arises from amendments corresponding to a previously issued notice of grounds for rejection — i.e., amendments submitted after notice create a new ground that requires examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisite: written amendment submitted in response to previous notice and the new rejection ground is found during amendment confirmation. Specific examples: (1) amendments to description/drawings add new matter or exceed permitted scope of divisional/conversion; (2) amendment of a claim previously examined results in lack of novelty or inventive step (unless that amended invention appears in another claim not previously notified — then non-final); (3) a newly generated or substantially changed claim equivalent to a newly-established claim contains novelty/inventive-step grounds; (4) after amendment an examiner discovers novelty/inventive-step grounds that were previously uneminable due to lack of clarity or added new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Rule Between Final and Non-final Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: When re-examining after amendment, issue a non-final notice unless all grounds for rejection clearly fall under the final notice criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain between the two types, issue non-final to preserve the applicant's amendment opportunity. The examiner should default to non-final except where all grounds are clearly final-type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on a Claim-by-claim Basis — Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner examines patentability requirements on a per-claim basis so that applicants can identify which claims are remediable and respond effectively; a single ground of rejection can block grant even if other claims are patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When notifying grounds for rejection in multi-claim applications, the examiner must specify the claim(s) containing grounds and provide specific explanations so applicants can determine which claims to amend or delete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Notice of Grounds for Rejection — Examination Outcomes (components)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written notice of grounds for rejection shall include [Examination Outcomes], comprised of: 'Claims to be Examined', 'Relevant Provision regarding Grounds for Rejection', 'Patentable Claims', and [Specific Grounds for Rejection]. Matters not being grounds but useful for response may be included in 'Considerations in Amendment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each component is described further below; include clear labelling and sufficient detail to allow applicant to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims to be Examined (in Notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall state the number of claims to be examined as of the date the written notice is prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the claim numbering current at preparation time; identify which claims are within the scope of the present examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant Provisions Regarding Grounds for Rejection (in Notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify which claims contain grounds for rejection and cite the relevant provisions of the Patent Act. If the ground is not directly related to claims, state the matter containing the ground. If amendment adds new matters or exceeds scope in divisional/converted applications, state those newly added or out-of-scope matters as grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a mapping (e.g., table) between notified matters and the corresponding Articles (examples given mapping description/claims to Articles 42(3), 42(8), 45, 29(2), 52(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable Claims (in Notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerate all claims not identified as grounds for rejection at the time of notice. This is not the examiner's final decision but a point-in-time indication of claims considered patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: do not list claims as patentable where special circumstances prevent assessment; claim judged unpatentable for grounds related to other matters; if not listed, explain reasons under 'Considerations in Amendment'. The examiner may later find new grounds and re-notify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Grounds for Rejection — Content and Level of Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Set out specific reasons for each notified ground of rejection so the applicant can understand and respond; indicate claims involved and the specific ground for each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: (i) Specifically state grounds for each claim; may summarize for claims with practically the same ground. (ii) When comparing cited inventions to claimed invention, indicate which parts of the cited invention correspond to which claimed features; select the closest cited invention and describe its technical features, point out differences, and state technical features of other cited inventions that supplement differences, with assessment considering common general knowledge. (iii) Examiner may specify the cited invention and describe differences and inventive-step assessment in an applicant-understandable manner. (iv) State novelty/inventive-step grounds for independent and dependent claims separately; for dependent claims, indicate corresponding matters of cited invention or assess differences based on common general knowledge. (v) Generally, dependent-claim grounds are deemed to include grounds identified in claims cited by dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Component Comparison Table
rubrics_metrics.description: Where necessary for comparison, prepare a component comparison table showing relations between distinguishing technical components of the claimed invention and corresponding features of the cited invention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the table state which features of cited documents correspond (with page/drawing references) and add an assessment of differences either within or below the table. If using multiple cited inventions, select the closest cited invention and, if needed, indicate how features of other cited inventions supplement differences (examples illustrate combining cited inventions 1 & 2 to show obviousness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in Amendment (in Notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include examiner opinions or matters not being grounds for rejection but useful for applicant's response, such as opinions about the description, reasons for excluding certain claims from 'Patentable Claims', and other amendment considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section can include matters not yet grounds for rejection but useful for future amendment submissions (e.g., for reexamination). Note: if examiner later intends to use content from 'Considerations in Amendment' as grounds, the examiner must re-notify the ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Written Decision of Rejection (format)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written decision of rejection is prepared with the same method as a written notice of grounds for rejection, except [Examination Outcomes] replaces 'matters notified for the ground for rejection' with 'matters where the ground for rejection is not overcome'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no written argument or amendment was submitted in response to a notice, examiner may omit separate [Examination Results] and [Rationale for Decision to Reject]. Include: 'Claims to be Examined', 'Relevant Provisions for Matters Where Grounds Not Overcome', 'Patentable Claims' (claims not notified and those where notified grounds have been overcome). Explain reasons when not listing patentable claims, and include 'Grounds for Decision to Reject' with specific rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Decision to Reject — required reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: When rendering a decision to reject, write more specific rationale regarding grounds not overcome so applicant can understand the basis; for claim-related grounds, state reasons by category of each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the same reasons were already notified in the prior written ground, the examiner may cite the source to avoid redundancy. When both written argument and amendment are submitted, explain why amendment/argument do not overcome the ground; for claims without practical amendments or dependent claims without direct amendments, a statement that 'the ground notified is not overcome' may suffice. When only a written argument without amendment is submitted, explain why applicant's argument is denied and state unresolved grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in Amendment Submission (post-decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: List issues not being grounds for rejection but useful for applicant when submitting written amendments or for subsequent procedures like requests for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: where decision to reject is based on previously-notified grounds but new grounds are produced by addition of claims or amendments, such matters can be included here to aid applicant's next response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for Examination on Claim-to-claim Basis — special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on handling claims in special circumstances on claim-by-claim examination: (1) claims related to a deficient detailed description may still be listed as patentable unless exceptions apply; (2) where a claim cites another claim that has a ground under Article 42(4), pay attention whether the citing claim still has that ground; (3) where an application has multiple groups of inventions, examiner considers patentability for at least one group and handles unity-of-invention rejections by indicating claims in other groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim is related to a notified detailed-description ground that cannot be remedied by amendment, explain in 'Considerations in Amendment Submission' why it is not listed as patentable. For citing claims, if the cited claim violates only manner of describing scope (Article 42(8) and Enforcement Order Article 5), state that only the cited claim has that ground. For multi-group inventions, include claims without grounds under 'Patentable Claims' for groups evaluated; if novelty/inventive-step grounds exist for those claims, notify both unity and patentability grounds. If lack of unity is prioritized for efficiency, state that patent requirements have not been tested for certain claims and do not include them as patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information on Prior Art Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing grounds for rejection related to a claim's technical subject matter, an examiner must cite supporting documents for the rationale; disclosure methods should comply with WIPO Standard ST.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite supporting patent and non-patent documents clearly and provide sufficient detail (see following citation rubrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Patent Documents — format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing patent documents as support for grounds, clearly state publishing country (may be omitted if Korea), title of patent document, document number (laid-open number), and publication date (public disclosure date if published in a gazette). Also clearly state which part (page/drawing) of the document is used for the citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles and document numbers are to be stated as in the patent documents. Examples given for Korea, US, Japan, UK, Germany and International publications; indicate page or drawing numbers or textual locus (e.g., 'Speed Reduction Gear', 'Drawing No. a,b,c'). Special notes for classification parentheticals for German patents and historical classification conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Non-patent Documents — bibliographic format
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing periodicals, non-periodicals, books, lectures or parts thereof, follow specified order and punctuation: Author, Title of Thesis, Title of Publication. Location: Publisher. Publication Date, Volume, Issue, Page No.; titles generally not abbreviated, and English publications use 'Vol. oo, No. oo'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: publication date may substitute volume number; month/year sufficient if no day; where unclear date, state date of obtaining; publisher name may be omitted if unnecessary; include country after location if obscure; for books follow similar order and use italics for book titles; indicate pages with 'pp.'; when citing a part, include page or drawing numbers in parentheses. Examples provided (Journal of Korean Chemistry Society; book entries; etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Electronic Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing electronic documents (CD-ROM, internet, on-line DB), state general information of cited document together with type of search medium (in braces), search date (in braces after publication date), and search site/URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the search medium and search date explicitly and include the Internet URL. Example given: author, title, organization, [online], date, [Search on July 15, 2010], Internet: <URL: http://...>.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/Reduction of Designated Period — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of KIPO or an examiner may, upon request, shorten or extend a designated period for patent procedures, or extend ex officio, deciding so in a way that does not unlawfully violate interests of interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision on whether to shorten/extend should balance interests; procedural details for substantive and formality examination periods are specified in the following rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Designated Period for Substantive Examination — rules and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions under Article 16 of the Enforcement Decree may be requested once or twice a month; requests of less than one month count as one month. Except for the period designated for written argument submission, such requests are deemed approved on filing, though examiner may partially approve/disapprove if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For extension requests affecting written argument submission: if extended expiry is within four months of original expiry, the request is deemed approved; beyond that, examiner reviews reasons and may approve for specified reasons (e.g., first appointment of attorney, change/ discharge of attorney within one month, change of applicants within one month when new applicants are added, receipt of foreign patent outcomes within two months and submission of them, delay in delivery of written grounds for more than one month, pending trial/litigation, necessary testing/evaluation, unavoidable reasons). Requests by third parties are not admitted for certain reasons. Fees must be paid; unpaid fee causes invalidation after an examiner-specified time limit; refunds occur when extension request is rejected or returned (procedural details included).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Period for Formality Examination — rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for amendment under Article 46 can be extended several times by month increments; a request under one month counts as one month; total extension shall not exceed four months except in special cases (reasons not attributable to applicant or international-stage entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extension request does not exceed four months and fee paid, it is deemed approved on filing; a 4-month approval carries a warning that no further extension will be approved. Subsequent extension requests after a 4-month approval are rejected. Overdue requests are returned with an opportunity to petition and fee refunded if returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of Designated Period and related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may request reduction of a designated period; when such request or a written amendment specifying reduction is submitted, the designated period is deemed expired as of the submission date. Other rules include single 30-day extension for requesting a trial against rejection (with possible further extension for persons in remote areas subject to IPT review), and returning amendments submitted after designated periods (except formalities amendments may be admitted before invalidation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial-request extension determinations and refund/return procedures are handled by IPT (Trial Policy Division) and examiners per rules; formalities amendments are more permissively admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for Written Argument — treatment and evidentiary scope
rubrics_metrics.description: When a written argument is submitted (with or without amendment), the examiner must review argument and amendment in depth to decide whether grounds for rejection are overcome. Written arguments and supporting documents (including experiment results) are not part of the specification but may be referred to in deciding patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment is submitted after designated period it shall be returned, but written arguments may be admitted as reference. If applicant's written argument claims amendments but fails to submit them, examiner examines based on the notification of ground for rejection; if actual amendments differ from those asserted in the argument, examination is based on actual amendments. Examiners must explain denials when only argument is submitted without amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Amendments — method to confirm final specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The final specification to be examined is determined automatically through the internal Patent Net after reflecting amendments to the detailed description, claims, and drawings. An amendment to the full text of the specification replaces the final specification to be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example process illustrated for multiple written amendments: the final specification reflects the most recent amendments for each part (detailed description, individual claims, drawings) as combined by the system; examiners should follow the system output to identify the text to be examined.
